scope.purpose: Separate owned-reader preparation/setup effects from its sequential-ingress allocation and process-resource effects while retaining the existing DOCX section-layout workload.
scope.cohort: 12 fresh-process matched owned_vec-versus-owned_reader pairs per binary arm (24 children per arm; 48 workload children across the normal and allocator-metrics arms), five warmups and 50 measured samples per child, CPU 12, alternating route order; descriptive attribution only.
scope.calibration_count: To be frozen by implementation preflight; no calibration children or final capture count are authorized by this design receipt.
unchanged_workload: same corpus, source/output digests, section selector, edit, commit and bounded sink
same semantic reopen, forward/inverse publication, preservation, source-freshness and limit/security checks
same per-sample route ownership: cloned archive input is prepared before open

observed_boundaries.finding: Preparation clones the 2,101,427-byte archive for both owned routes, then creates route observers and reserves the bounded sink before preparation timing ends.
Owned-reader preparation additionally allocates two Arc<AtomicU64> read observers; sink reserve is shared route setup, not reader-specific.
Open timing contains owned-vector from_vec and owned-reader from_reader; query/edit/commit/publication remain separate.
OwnedIngressReader retains the cloned Vec in Cursor and counts read calls and bytes.
from_reader consumes the reader through read_limited and then moves the resulting Vec into OwnedSource; from_vec moves the supplied Vec directly.
read_limited reserves an initial chunk and then try_reserve_exact(read) for each successful read, so reader open has a distinct ingest/growth interval.
The existing allocator Sample exposes call/byte/live/peak fields; Region::split publishes a non-overlapping segment while retaining the combined region.
Existing process snapshots expose minor/major faults, CPU ticks, context switches, I/O counters and RSS deltas, with documented procfs probe overhead.

experiment.builds: Build a normal reference and an allocator-metrics diagnostic binary from identical source, compiler, profile, corpus and environment; bind both binary hashes. Do not use diagnostic elapsed values as production latency evidence.
experiment.region_1: Begin the existing allocation Region immediately before the owned-input clone at preparation start; split immediately after sink.reserve_budget and the existing preparation endpoint.
experiment.region_2: Keep the same Region active through the existing open operation and finish_split at the existing open endpoint. Preserve the combined sample as a consistency check.
experiment.process_observation: Take process_metrics snapshots immediately outside each segment boundary and report deltas for minor/major faults, user/system CPU, context switches, rchar/syscr, read_bytes and RSS. Keep procfs snapshot time and region-boundary overhead out of the route phase timer where the harness permits, and report probe overhead explicitly.
experiment.existing_route_counters: Retain owned-reader read_calls/read_bytes and the existing phase vectors; do not add a replacement reader or bypass read_limited.
experiment.calibration: Run the same boundary and process-snapshot sequence around a black_box-only calibration body and report its boundary/observer cost. Also retain matched normal-versus-diagnostic binary identity; never subtract either calibration from production phase values.
output: per-sample prep and open allocation Samples including status, calls, bytes, live and peak fields
per-segment process deltas and existing reader read-call/read-byte counters
existing total and six phase timings, phase sums, child/pair/order metadata and sample_order
instrumentation identity, calibration cost and unavailable/overflow statuses

interpretation.reader_open_copy_signal: Reader-open allocation/reallocation bytes and calls near the input length, together with its existing read_bytes, would support the bounded statement that sequential ingestion performs additional materialization/growth relative to from_vec.
interpretation.prep_outlier_signal: If reader and vector preparation allocation samples are similar but reader elapsed outliers coincide with process fault or CPU deltas, the result is consistent with page-touch or host-resource effects; if allocation/CPU differs without fault differences, it is consistent with setup/copy work.
limits: Allocator callbacks and boundary observers can perturb scheduling and allocation; diagnostic timings are descriptive only.
Procfs fault, CPU, I/O and RSS deltas include probe effects and are not phase-local physical-cause measurements.
The existing read-byte counter measures reader transfer volume, not memcpy cycles; this plan cannot prove a memcpy-only cause.
No result may be attributed to glibc, allocator arenas, ASLR, page faults, scheduler or frequency without separate evidence.
Use sample_order to reconstruct chronology; elapsed-rank vectors alone do not preserve execution order.
No production gate, adoption decision, threshold relaxation or population claim follows from this diagnostic cohort.
